title: Bringing it home
hook: all the year's learning into one day's shape

segments.voice: Yesterday: art and music debates, two girls singing on Eid and a flute of the family of David. Your line was views differ, voices rise. The questions of today are done; now, a practice for today.

A river runs past your front door. That's the picture the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, gives his companions in Sahih al-Bukhari. Suppose, he says, in paraphrase, there were a river at someone's door, and he bathed in it five times a day. Would any dirt be left on him? None at all, they say. That, he says, is the five prayers: through them Allah wipes away wrongs. Not one great washing a year. A river, at the door, every day.
screen: `A RIVER AT THE DOOR.` → `FIVE TIMES A DAY.` → `A RIVER, EVERY DAY.`

segments.voice: Start where the day starts, with intention. The first report in Sahih al-Bukhari says, in paraphrase, that actions are judged by their intentions, and each person gets what they intended. So a day begins before the alarm is off: what is today for? Then the frame. The Qur'an gives it in the chapter called Hud, in Pickthall's translation: "Establish worship at the two ends of the day and in some watches of the night. Lo! good deeds annul ill deeds." The two ends of the day: dawn and dusk, with prayers in between, so that work, school, errands and meals all happen inside a frame, the way a river runs between its banks. Inside that frame go the small things this path has been collecting: the bismillah before eating, the greeting of peace, a word kept kind, a debt remembered, a coin set aside, a minute of Qur'an. None of them is large. That's the point of the last piece. Al-Bukhari keeps a saying, reported by 'Aisha, that the deeds most loved by Allah are the ones done regularly, even if they are small. Not the heroic weekend. The steady weekday. So the shape of a whole day, in this tradition, is not a schedule of impressive acts. It's an intention at the start, a frame of prayer, small good deeds in the gaps, and a return to the river, again and again. What comes home from a year of learning, in this picture, is not a pile of facts. It's a day with a shape.
screen: `FIRST, THE INTENTION.` · `THE TWO ENDS OF THE DAY.` · `SMALL GOOD THINGS IN THE GAPS.` · `REGULAR, EVEN IF SMALL.` · then, large: `A RIVER AT THE DOOR.`

segments.voice: Picture waking up tomorrow and the first thing you'd like to intend, then move through the day in your mind, placing one small thing at each part: a prayer if you pray, a breath, a kind word, a moment of thanks, a few verses read. Keep each one small enough to really do. Then picture lying down at night, the day done, the frame held.
Bringing it home. Gathering a year's learning into one day's shape: an intention, the frame of prayer, small good deeds done regularly. Today's word.
Your line: a day, whole. Small, regular, and held in a frame. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims shape the day around the daily prayers, from dawn to night, and fill the time between with work, family and small acts of worship such as remembrance of Allah, reading the Qur'an and giving.

chat.says: After a whole year of learning, what's the point if I can't remember it all?
options: The point is a day with a shape: an intention, prayer, and small deeds done regularly.
Memorize it all; the deeds most loved are the biggest and most heroic ones.
Then start over; only one great effort a year really wipes away wrongs.
chat.meaning: The deeds most loved by Allah are the regular ones, even if small. A year's learning comes home as a day with a shape, like a river at the door.
